paragraphs.text: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia. It causes short-trunk short stature that becomes noticeable in childhood. Intelligence and facies are normal. Radiographic features include rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of the rib cartilages, short femoral necks, and mildly shortened metacarpals. Epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones vary between patients (Miyake et al., 2012). Miyake et al. (2012) concluded that PAPSS2 mutations produce a skeletal dysplasia family with a gradation of phenotypes ranging from brachyolmia to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large, inbred, 8-generation kindred from a remote area of Pakistan with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD). They evaluated 16 affected individuals (11 males and 5 females). Clinical findings were short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence. Radiographs showed the following: - delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees - platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces - diffuse early osteoarthritic changes, mainly in the spine and hands - mild brachydactyly - mild metaphyseal abnormalities, mostly at the hips and knees

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) described 6 patients with autosomal recessive brachyolmia: 3 affected members of a Turkish family, 2 Japanese patients, and 1 Korean patient. The patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood, with normal intelligence and facies. Radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of the rib cartilages, short femoral necks, and mildly shortened metacarpals. The spinal changes were very similar in all 6 patients, whereas the epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones varied.

paragraphs.text: In 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia, Miyake et al. (2012) used exon capture followed by next-generation sequencing. They identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the PAPSS2 gene, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18). In 3 additional patients with a similar brachyolmia phenotype (2 Japanese and 1 Korean), they found PAPSS2 mutations as follows: - 1 patient was homozygous for a splice site mutation (IVS3+2delT). - 1 patient was compound heterozygous for 2 loss-of-function mutations, c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19). - 1 patient was compound heterozygous for 2 loss-of-function mutations, c.480_481insCGTA (p.K161RfsX6) and c.661delA (p.I221SfsX40).
